body.estimand_functional: Put \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\) and \(b_n=n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) when \(d\leq4t\), while \(b_n=n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) when \(d>4t\). The proved all-regime statement is \(c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). On the proved no-penalty subregion \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), \(\rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\). The complete all-regime frontier and the necessary direction of the propensity comparison remain open; \(r_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) is not defined.

sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed observed margins of a law in \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A\) has unknown propensity \(e\) under the observational experiment; the comparison experiment supplies the exact function \(e_P\) to the test.
sampling_model.outcome: Observed and potential outcomes are binary. The pointwise restrictions \(m_0,m_1\in[1/4,3/4]\) apply to the canonical continuous representatives of the two conditional-mean equivalence classes.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator and no nuisance convergence rate is part of the class; all tuning is a deterministic function of \(n,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives the pointwise CATE-estimation minimax rate with a nuisance-smoothness elbow, and Theorem 2 gives attainability under additional design-density conditions.
Theorems 4 and 6 give fixed-alternative consistency and a local weak limit for quantitative homogeneity tests over structured rule classes under the paper's nuisance conditions.

Theorems 1--2 establish asymptotic normality for propensity-reweighted pairwise and multisample adjusted \(U\)-statistics under consistent propensity estimation, independent stratum samples, stable positive sample fractions, and pointwise overlap.

Section 3 derives joint asymptotic normality and Gaussian-simulation calibration for multisample \(U\)-statistics testing equality of additive treatment effects across a fixed collection of mutually independent prespecified strata.

Theorem 6 gives asymptotic level, fixed-alternative consistency, and nontrivial \(n^{-1/2}\)-local power for a multiplier-bootstrap test of homogeneous restricted CATE with possibly right-censored duration outcomes.

Section 4 gives a conservative finite-sample-valid Fisher randomization test for the sharp null of one unknown constant individual treatment effect by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over a confidence set for that nuisance effect.

The main martingale-transformation results give asymptotic level for a permutation test of a constant marginal-distribution shift with an estimated nuisance shift, retaining exact level only for the more restrictive sharp null.
Theorems 3 and 7 give asymptotic chi-square tests of equality of finitely many score-defined group average treatment effects under complete randomization, with sample splitting or cross-fitting.
Theorems 4.1 and 5.2 give matching nonasymptotic binned conditional-independence critical radii for fixed discrete responses and a continuous conditioning variable under total-variation smoothness.
Theorems 6 and 7 give null validity and spline minimax power for projected conditional covariance under common smoothness and nondegeneracy restrictions.
Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 characterize bias, variance, and optimal separate wavelet resolutions for estimating a signed expected conditional covariance functional.
The main minimax theorems derive sharp heteroskedasticity-detection rates using a squared first-difference proxy under a rough unknown mean.
Theorem 1 gives asymptotic normality and type-I error control for an intra-fold split CATE-variance statistic under explicit nuisance learner-rate conditions.
The paper proves that the propensity score is ancillary for semiparametrically efficient estimation of the regular average treatment effect under ignorability.
Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 give asymptotic null validity and consistency against smooth local sieve alternatives for the null that the conditional average treatment effect is constant.

The paper develops \(L_1\)-type tests based on uniformly consistent nonparametric kernel estimators for conditional treatment-effect restrictions and proves asymptotically correct size, fixed-alternative consistency, and power against some local alternatives.
Section 1 records the classical nonadaptive Hölder goodness-of-fit boundary, and the paper establishes the iterated-logarithmic price of adaptation in wavelet testing.

body.tldr: The proved result is presently an honest all-regime bracket for the fixed-sample observational critical radius, together with the classical known-propensity benchmark and a matched no-penalty subregion. With \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\), the critical radius lies between \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\) and the explicit single-scale rate \(n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) for \(d\leq4t\), or \(n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) for \(d>4t\). If \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), both bounds equal the known-propensity order \(n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\). Exact likelihood expansion of a nested macro--fine repair verifies one-observation matching and exposes the first residual fixed-sample collision coefficient, but the bounded moment system, matching sparse-occupancy test, and all-regime optimization remain open. The failed frozen optimizations are retained only as diagnostics, and no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

project_justification.gap: Existing homogeneity tests provide asymptotic validity, fixed-direction power, or finite-stratum comparisons, while existing minimax work concerns different testing geometries or pointwise CATE estimation. On the identical binary uniform-design causal class, the unresolved object is still a matching fixed-sample lower and upper detection map across all three Hölder indices and all occupancy regimes.
project_justification.niche: The live mathematical niche is the likelihood-level interaction between an unknown constant-effect null, separate propensity and baseline roughness, macro-scale CATE variation, and fine-scale repeated-observation collisions. Any sharp result must preserve exact uniform design, keep every null-prior component homogeneous, and account for every correction factor involving the CATE perturbation.
project_justification.fill: The established contribution supplies an explicit total single-scale fourth-order test, an all-regime upper bound, the known-propensity benchmark, and a matched no-penalty subregion. The current likelihood audit adds an exact nested one-observation identity and an explicit two-observation early-kill coefficient. These results delimit, but do not solve, the remaining task of constructing bounded moment-matched priors and a matching nested corrected-energy test.

(2008) & Unconfounded treatment with growing series regressions & \(\tau(x)=c\) & Smooth sieve departures & Asymptotic size and consistency only.\\ Sant'Anna (2021) & Iid right-censored durations under unconfoundedness, with a binary-IV extension & Restricted CATE is constant almost surely & Fixed and \(n^{-1/2}\)-local integrated-moment alternatives & Theorem 6 is asymptotic; multiplier-bootstrap calibration is not uniform finite-sample.\\ Dai--Stern (2022) & Mutually independent treatment and control samples in finitely many prespecified strata & Additive treatment effects are equal across strata & Pairwise multisample \(U\)-functionals & Section 3 uses joint asymptotic normality and Gaussian simulation, not finite-sample uniform calibration.\\ Dai--Shen--Stern (2023) & Independent observational strata reweighted by estimated propensities & Average treatment effects are equal across strata & Adjusted multisample \(U\)-functionals & Theorems 1--2 give asymptotic normality under consistent propensity estimation and stable stratum fractions.\\ Ding--Feller--Miratrix (2016) & Fixed potential outcomes under a known randomized assignment & One unknown constant individual treatment effect, or a specified finite-dimensional effect model & Distributional test statistics under Fisher randomization & The confidence-set maximized test is finite-sample valid but targets a sharp unit-level null.\\ Chung--Olivares (2021) & Two randomized samples from marginal outcome distributions & The treated distribution is an unknown constant shift of the control distribution & Supremum distance after martingale transformation & General validity is asymptotic; exactness is retained only for the sharper known-shift null.\\ Imai--Li (2025) & Iid units with complete randomization and an external or split-sample score & A fixed number of score-defined group average effects are equal & Finite-dimensional GATE contrasts & Theorems 3 and 7 give asymptotic chi-square calibration, not an omnibus continuous-CATE guarantee.\\ Dukes et al. (2026) & Observational causal model with a structured rule class and estimated nuisances & Quantitative CATE homogeneity over that rule class & Structured policy-direction contrasts & Theorems 2, 4, and 6 give asymptotic size, fixed power, and local weak limits.\\ Yu (2026) & Observational causal model with learner-rate and nondegeneracy conditions & \(\operatorname{Var}\{\tau(X)\}=0\) & Fixed positive CATE variance & Theorem 1 is asymptotic and assumes nuisance rates.\\ Chang et al. (2015) & Unconfounded treatment with kernel conditional-mean estimators & Zero, nonpositive, or distributional conditional-effect restrictions & \(L_1\)-type fixed and local alternatives & Asymptotically correct size and consistency only.\\ NBW (2021) & Discrete responses and a continuous conditioner with conditional-law smoothness & Conditional independence & Total-variation distance to the null class & Theorems 4.1 and 5.2 give nonasymptotic minimax bounds in a different model.\\ PCM (2024) & Conditional-mean model with spline regressions and common smoothness & Conditional mean independence & Squared projected conditional mean & Theorems 6--7 give uniform asymptotic, not finite-sample, guarantees. \end{tabular}\end{center} SantAnna2021, Section 4.2 and Theorem 6, is the closest continuous-covariate extension of the Crump constant-CATE null, but its censored-duration integrated moments and root-\(n\) directional alternatives do not define a three-index Hölder minimax radius. DaiStern2022, Section 3, and DaiShenStern2023, Theorems 1--2, compare average effects across a fixed finite stratum geometry; neither tests arbitrary variation over the full-support cube nor provides uniform finite-sample calibration. DingFellerMiratrix2016 supplies exact-design validity for a sharper unit-level constant-effect null, ChungOlivares2021 supplies asymptotic distribution-shift permutation validity, and ImaiLi2025 tests equality of finitely many score-defined GATEs; these nulls can respectively be stronger than, different from, or coarser than continuous CATE constancy. CrumpHotzImbensMitnik2008 remains the closest uncensored unknown-constant-CATE predecessor, but its series asymptotics do not furnish the present fixed-sample radius. ChangLeeWhang2015 and DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026 establish asymptotic conditional-effect tests under kernel or structured-rule formulations. Yu2026VarianceHTE studies the same variance-zero characterization under supplied learner rates. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 concerns pointwise CATE estimation; its loss and support-modified lower construction do not solve global homogeneity testing. NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 and LundborgKimShahSamworth2024 supply testing machinery under different null manifolds and metrics. McGrathMukherjee2026 informs separate nuisance resolutions for a signed covariance functional, and KotekalKundu2025 informs rough-regression proxy design under a Gaussian likelihood. Spokoiny1996 supplies only the known-propensity goodness-of-fit benchmark, and Hahn1998 supplies only the regular ATE ancillarity comparator.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The frozen mixture envelope is invalid as a universal converse handle because a legal positive-CATE tuple is hidden in its nominal high-order remainder, and the frozen testing envelope is not sharp because it turns an unconditional first-projection floor into a fourth-root distance loss. In the nested repair, the exact binary likelihood equals a propensity factor times an arm-regression factor. The alternative CATE correction therefore also generates a propensity-times-CATE term. Conditional one-observation matching follows from the covariance equation and the smooth square-partition identity, but the simplest bounded Rademacher coefficient laws leave, after outer-sign averaging, a two-observation fine-collision residual of the form \(-\delta^2 k_1k_2(1+q_e^2x_1x_2)\). At \(d=\gamma=1\) and \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), this residual is subdominant at the candidate four-collision scale \(\delta\asymp n^{-4/15}\), whereas any uncancelled macro term of scale \(n^2H\delta^4\) diverges. The remaining moment equations, all-order support remainder, and matching upper collision projections have not been solved.
body.honest_scope: The causal estimand remains the centered \(L^2\) norm of the CATE, and the statistical class remains the original binary uniform-design Hölder class with fixed overlap and interior margins. The known-propensity rate is a standard comparator and carries no novelty claim. The proved observational content is the all-regime bracket and the sufficient no-penalty region; smoothness adaptation is not claimed. The old deterministic mixture and testing optimizations are regression tests for invalid envelopes, not definitions of the minimax radius. The complete rough-nuisance frontier, equality-case logarithms outside the proved region, and the necessary-and-sufficient propensity-value frontier remain open. No conclusion certifies a fitted forest, and non-rejection is not evidence that the CATE is constant.
